protocol.ranking: expectancy in R, not win rate

verdict.headline: NO EDGE FOUND — do not trade this configuration
verdict.summary: Across 1,056 evaluations (96 entry configurations × 11 stop/exit models) on 1,001,451 real bars, not one configuration reached positive expectancy even on the training slice it was fitted to. The best in-sample result was -0.115R per trade. The configuration selected on validation then scored -0.364R with a profit factor of 0.49 on the untouched holdout.
verdict.recommendation: Runs in paper-research mode only so forward evidence keeps accumulating. It is not promoted, not weighted in any ranking, and must not be treated as a validated edge. Promotion would require positive out-of-sample expectancy on a materially larger sample.
caveats: Win rate and profit factor can look acceptable while expectancy in R is negative: profit factor is percentage-weighted, expectancy is risk-normalised. Under fixed-fractional sizing the risk-normalised figure is the one that governs outcomes.
1-minute and 3-minute bars are not entitled on the current data plan, so those timeframes are untested rather than assumed to behave the same way.
Costs are non-zero throughout: 0.05% slippage per fill plus 0.02% commission per side.
